description: API-listener liveness and readiness probes. Both are tier 2 in the ledger (operational); wave 1 baselines them because the native clients' server picker and the cluster health checks read them before any login.

rows.tier2_inclusion: Operational probe consumed by the multi-server picker on Apple/Android before authentication; wave 1 covers discovery.

not_applicable.authorization: Public liveness probe; no principal distinction exists.
not_applicable.error: The handler has no failure branch; it never inspects dependencies.
not_applicable.raw_protocol: Plain JSON; no ranges, redirects, or upgrades.

scenarios.description: Liveness answers 200 with a JSON body even when the database is unreachable; it checks nothing.
The body carries the configured server name and stable server id so a client can label and de-duplicate servers.
Exactly status, server_name, and server_id are present; identity fields are omitted (not null) when unconfigured.
scenarios.notes: Omission-on-empty (omitempty) rather than explicit null; the section PR decides whether v2 keeps optional-absent for identity.

rows.tier2_inclusion: Readiness gate used by cluster orchestration and the server picker; wave 1 covers discovery.

not_applicable.authorization: Public readiness probe; no principal distinction exists.
not_applicable.raw_protocol: Plain JSON; no ranges, redirects, or upgrades.

scenarios.description: With Postgres reachable and no S3 configured, readiness is 200 and reports only status.
With Postgres unreachable, readiness is 503 and the per-dependency booleans appear.
The dependency booleans are present only on failure; a healthy answer omits them rather than reporting true.
scenarios.notes: Asymmetric shape: booleans exist only when status is error. Flagged for the section PR; an unconfigured S3 reports as healthy (true).

scenarios.description: status is the aggregate of the dependency checks: error exactly when any dependency fails.
